intended_object: An auxiliary construction: the character χ_d of the compact group X × Y (built via ZMod.toCircle), viewed as an element of L²(X × Y, productHaar). It exists only to assemble the Fourier Hilbert basis `splitFourierBasis` in the paper's Connes-rigidity construction. Inferred from the body and its use; the docstring is generic boilerplate.
explanation: The body is just `ContinuousMap.toLp 2 productHaar ℂ (splitComplexCharacter d)`. It takes the continuous character z ↦ toCircle(z.1 d.1 + z.2 d.2) on X × Y = (V →ₗ[F] F) × (B →ₗ[F] F) and views it as an L² class. Its only role is as scaffolding for the Hilbert basis: the next results prove density of span (`splitCharacterL2_span_closure_eq_top`) and orthonormality (`splitCharacterL2_orthonormal`), and these feed `splitFourierBasis` via `HilbertBasis.mk`. The docstring is the file-wide boilerplate "Cross-module support…". The definition is tied to one concrete internal setup (F = ZMod 2, specific spaces V and B). It is a thin wrapper around a Mathlib coercion, not a standalone mathematical notion. As a construction it is correct: characters are continuous and Haar measure is finite here, so `toLp` applies. Mathlib's analogous `fourierLp` covers only the additive circle, so there is no general Mathlib counterpart.
